mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation rate (CPIAUCSL below 3.0%) indicates stable monetary conditions that reduce uncertainty and support positive equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods where CPIAUCSL is below 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0% over the 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% within the last month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0% over the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS above 150,000 thousand) indicates robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 thousand.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns when both series decline, as evidenced by a Rank IC below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals an impending slowdown in consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansions when HOUST declines.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a severe supply-side shock that disrupts corporate supply chains and reduces earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between INDPRO and GDPC1 fails to predict negative returns when both decline, as shown by a Rank IC below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) accelerates the reduction in liquidity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 45% of periods during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS is rising.
